1. What the module does

The module measures the neurites of each cell in fluorescence images of live neurons with a cell-fill marker (for XDP: RGEDI, EGFP fill in the FITC channel). It works with images from any microscope. The default settings read ImageXpress (IXM) files; five settings describe other file names, tile grids and tile overlaps (section 5a). For each well and timepoint it does these steps:

raw tiles (any grid), or one stitched image→ image correction per tile→ whole-well montage→ Cellpose-SAM cell bodies (somas)→ clDice U-Net neurite map→ each neurite assigned to the soma it grows from→ percell.csv + perwell.csv + QC overlay
  • Montage, not tiles. Neurites that cross a tile edge are traced as one piece.
  • Image correction: each tile is flattened and normalised before stitching, and detections on the tile seams are removed. This stops the tile edges from being segmented as neurites. See 1a.
  • Somas: Cellpose-SAM on each raw tile, with a debris filter.
  • Neurites: a small U-Net trained with the clDice loss on 12 crops that we traced by hand in Fiji (SNT). On held-out crops it scored F1 0.645, against 0.135 for the old Frangi filter. Section 8 shows how it was trained.
  • Attribution: a neurite counts for a soma only if it leaves that soma outward (root-contact rule). A neighbour's neurite that only touches the soma is not counted.
  • Measurements per cell: total neurite length, skeleton pixels, branch points, tips, primary neurites, longest path.
  • Cache: the slow GPU part (somas + neurite map) is saved per well. Later runs with new post-segmentation settings use the cache and need only a CPU.
Why the main script is ml/neurite/montage_percell.py It is the script that made the final XDP neurite results. The name says what it does: it builds the whole-well montage and reports results per cell. It lives in ml/neurite/, next to the model code it uses (percell_integrate.py, model.py), not in bin/ with the Nextflow modules. bin/neurite_montage.py is an older database version of the same idea, with different numbers (section 10).

1a. Image correction: why tile seams are not segmented as neurites

Each raw tile is darker at its edges than in its middle (vignetting), and tiles differ in background and brightness. When tiles are put side by side, this makes dark lines and steps at every seam. The neurite model looks for thin bright lines, so without correction it would trace the seams as long, straight, false neurites. The module corrects the image in four steps. The first three run on each tile before stitching, and only on the image used for neurites:

  1. Flatten the illumination (--flatten-size 128). The smooth background of each tile (vignetting and haze) is estimated and subtracted. The estimate ignores objects smaller than about 128 px, so somas and neurites stay. No flat-field reference image is needed.
  2. Empty-tile guard. A tile with almost no signal (less than 15% of the typical tile's range) is set to zero. Otherwise step 3 would stretch its noise into a bright false tile.
  3. Normalise each tile to the range 0–1 between its own 1st and 99.5th percentile. This removes exposure differences between tiles, and it is the same normalisation that the model was trained with.
  4. Remove detections on the seams (--seam-band 6), after the neurite map is made. A sharp line stays exactly at each seam (see the close-up below), so neurite pixels within 6 px of a seam are removed. A real neurite that crosses a seam loses only those 12 px, which is small for its length. With OVERLAP_PX, the seams are the cut lines (5a).

Somas are found on the uncorrected raw tiles. Cellpose-SAM works well on raw tiles, so the correction changes only the neurite image. A debris filter (--clean-k 2.0) then removes objects that are not clearly brighter than the background (by 2 robust standard deviations). For images with strong vignetting, where dim cells at the tile edges are missed, --soma-flatten 128 runs Cellpose on flattened tiles too (it was not used for XDP).

Keep --flatten-size 128 and --seam-band 6. The job scripts set both. If you run montage_percell.py by hand, set them yourself: the script's own default for --flatten-size is 0 (off). If you see straight lines along tile edges in an overlay, check these two settings first.

The full methods text is in docs/METHODS_neurite_quantification.md.

3. One-time setup

3a. Cluster access

  1. Get a cluster account in the finkbeinerlab group, and ScaleFT (sft) on your computer. Ask Gladstone IT.
  2. Enroll once: sft enroll (team gladstone, in your browser). If a command later says “Authentication token expired”, run sft unenroll and then sft enroll again.
  3. Log in to the dev node: sft ssh fb-galaxy-dev01. To run one command without logging in: sft ssh --command '<command>' fb-galaxy-dev01. The remote command must use --command.
The dev node is shared and has no GPU. Use it only to edit files, run git, and submit jobs. Run all real work as a Slurm job (sbatch) on the galaxy partition.

3b. Get the code on the cluster

On fb-galaxy-dev01:

git clone -b austin-claude https://github.com/finkbeiner-lab/nextflow-cluster.git ~/nextflow-cluster
cd ~/nextflow-cluster && git log --oneline -1
The container is not in the clone. Git does not store the 9.3 GB container image. Everything on this branch finds the lab-shared copy by itself: the neurite job scripts use /gladstone/finkbeiner/kaye/XDP/dev-nextflow-modules/nextflow-cluster.sif, and run.sh uses it when your checkout has no nextflow-cluster.sif (the job log then starts with a NOTE that says so). To use a different image, pass SIF=/path/to.sif (job scripts) or NEXTFLOW_SIF=/path/to.sif (run.sh). Do not use the older image in steve/work/projects/nextflow-cluster/: it does not have this module.

Code may live in your cluster home. Outputs may not. Write all outputs to a lab project folder on the HIVE, for example /gladstone/finkbeiner/<PI-or-project>/<your-folder>/. Raw image folders under /gladstone/finkbeiner/robodata/ are read-only: never write there.

3c. Check that you can read the shared files

ls -l /gladstone/finkbeiner/kaye/XDP/dev-nextflow-modules/nextflow-cluster.sif \
      /gladstone/finkbeiner/kaye/XDP/dev-nextflow-modules/neurite-model-runs/run1/best.pt \
      /gladstone/finkbeiner/kaye/XDP/neurite-rework/example-test/

If you get “Permission denied”, ask IT to add you to the finkbeinerlab group.

4. Reproduce the example output (do this first)

The example is two wells from experiment XDP5 at timepoint T7: one control well and one XDP well. These are real wells from the final published run, so you can compare your numbers with ours.

C0333114.CCTR197674467.30.90

Test 1CPU, from the cache (about 5 minutes)

This checks your code checkout, the container and the model path. The numbers must be identical.

mkdir -p ~/neurite-jobs && cd ~/neurite-jobs
sbatch --export=ALL,OUT=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<your-lab-folder>/neurite-example-test \
       ~/nextflow-cluster/ml/neurite/sbatch/neurite_example_cpu.sbatch

Test 2GPU, from the raw images (about 10 minutes when it runs)

This is the full path you will use for new data. It needs a GPU, so it can wait in the queue for a while.

cd ~/neurite-jobs
sbatch --export=ALL,OUT=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<your-lab-folder>/neurite-example-test \
       ~/nextflow-cluster/ml/neurite/sbatch/neurite_example_gpu.sbatch

Watch the jobs and read the result

squeue -o "%.8i %.10u %.14j %.9P %.8T %.10M %.9l %.6D %.10b %R" -S -t,i
cat ~/neurite-jobs/nrt_example_cpu_*.out
cat ~/neurite-jobs/nrt_example_gpu_*.out

The last line of each log is RESULT: PASS or RESULT: FAIL. Test 1 must pass exactly. Test 2 allows 5% per column, because the GPU can give very small differences (in our own check, one I03 cell more had a neurite: 1799 instead of 1798). For test 2, also open <OUT>/gpu_from_raw/latest/XDP5_C03_T7_percell.tif in Fiji and compare it with the overlay in expected/.

Both tests pass? Your setup is correct, and you can run your own data.

5. Run the module on your own data (any microscope)

5a. Describe your images

The module needs one image channel per well and timepoint: the cell fill (morphology) channel. It can read it as a grid of tiles or as one already-stitched image. Five settings tell it where the files are and how the tiles fit together. The defaults read IXM data like the XDP experiments, so for IXM you set nothing.

Job-script settingScript optionDefault (IXM)What it means
WELL_DIR--well-dir{raw_folder}/{well}Folder of one well, under RAW_ROOT. Use . if all images are in RAW_ROOT itself.
TILE_PATTERN--tile-pattern*_{tp}_*_{well}_{site}_FITC_*.tifFile names of the cell-fill channel. {well}, {tp}, {experiment} are filled in from the manifest. {site} is the tile number. * means “any text”.
GRID--grid4x4Tiles per well as ROWSxCOLUMNS, for example 3x3, 5x5, 3x5. 1x1 = one stitched image.
TILE_ORDER--tile-orderstandardHow the microscope scans the tiles (picture below).
OVERLAP_PX--overlap-px0Pixels shared by neighbouring tiles. 0 = tiles touch edge to edge.

The folder placeholders are {experiment}, {well}, {tp} and {raw_folder} (the manifest column). A well must have exactly ROWS×COLUMNS matching files, or it is skipped with a message that says how many it found and where. The tiles are put in place by their site number, lowest first; the numbers can start at 0 or 1.

Examples. The file names in examples 2 and 3 are made up; adapt the pattern to yours.

Your dataSettings
IXM, 16 sites, FITC (the XDP data)Nothing. The defaults.
Snake scan, 5×5 tiles, 186 px overlap, files like B02_T5_s07_GFP.tif in <RAW_ROOT>/<plate>/ WELL_DIR={raw_folder}
TILE_PATTERN={well}_{tp}_s{site}_GFP.tif
GRID=5x5 TILE_ORDER=serpentine OVERLAP_PX=186
One stitched image per well, files like montage_B02_T5.tif WELL_DIR=. TILE_PATTERN=montage_{well}_{tp}.tif GRID=1x1
  • Check the pattern first. On the dev node, list one well folder (ls <folder> | head) and compare a file name with your pattern. Then run 1–2 wells and read the log before a full plate.
  • Other channels in the same folder are fine. The pattern picks only the cell-fill channel.
  • Image size and objective. The neurite model and the soma size (--diameter 25) were set on 20X images at about 0.35 µm per pixel. Other objectives, markers or cell types need a check (section 11), and maybe a retrained model (section 8).

5b. Make a manifest

One row per well. One timepoint per row; to measure several timepoints, add one row per (well, timepoint).

experiment,well,timepoint,cell_line,genotype,raw_folder
MYEXP,B02,T5,lineA,CTR,MYEXP-plate1
MYEXP,B03,T5,lineB,XDP,MYEXP-plate1
  • timepoint must be written exactly as it is in your file names (T5, t005, …): it fills {tp}.
  • cell_line and genotype are only copied to the output. Use any labels.
  • raw_folder fills {raw_folder}. If you leave the column out, it becomes <experiment>-RGEDI (the XDP folder names).
  • Put the manifest in your lab project folder.

5c. Submit

For IXM data:

cd ~/neurite-jobs
sbatch --time=10:00:00 \
  --export=ALL,MANIFEST=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<lab-folder>/<project>/manifest.csv,RAW_ROOT=/gladstone/finkbeiner/robodata/<scope>/<user>,OUT=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<lab-folder>/<project>/neurite,LABEL=first \
  ~/nextflow-cluster/ml/neurite/sbatch/neurite_run.sbatch

For other data, add the settings from 5a. Set them with export first: sbatch --export splits on commas, and the quotes keep the braces safe.

export WELL_DIR='{raw_folder}' TILE_PATTERN='{well}_{tp}_s{site}_GFP.tif' GRID=5x5 TILE_ORDER=serpentine OVERLAP_PX=186
sbatch --time=10:00:00 --export=ALL,MANIFEST=...,RAW_ROOT=...,OUT=...,LABEL=first \
  ~/nextflow-cluster/ml/neurite/sbatch/neurite_run.sbatch

The log prints the settings it used (input: ...), and params.json records them.

  • Time: about 4–5 minutes per 16-tile well on a V100 GPU (more tiles take longer). Set --time to that plus margin. If the job runs out of time, submit it again with the same OUT: finished wells come from the cache in about a minute each.
  • Start small. Run 2–4 wells first and look at the overlays before you run a full plate.
  • One well fails? The log shows FAILED or SKIP for that well and the job goes on with the next one. SKIP: found N tiles (need M for a RxC grid) in <folder> means the folder, pattern, well or timepoint does not match your files.

5d. Change settings later without the GPU

The cache keeps soma labels and the neurite map. You can change the neurite threshold, --seam-band, --min-neurite, --soma-dilation and the attribution settings (--root-px, --min-radial, --cross-cos) and recompute on a CPU node: same OUT, a new LABEL, DEVICE=cpu, and remove the --gres line. Each run goes to its own folder OUT/runs/<timestamp>_<LABEL>/; earlier runs are never overwritten.

Soma settings (--diameter, --flow, --cellprob, --clean-k, --soma-*), --flatten-size, the tile layout (grid, order, overlap) and the checkpoint are saved inside the cache. If you change them, use a new cache folder. The script refuses a cache that was made with different settings.

Cache runs do not write overlays. To make overlays for a cache run (CPU only; the layout settings are read from the run's params.json):

apptainer exec -B /gladstone/finkbeiner:/gladstone/finkbeiner <SIF> \
  python ~/nextflow-cluster/ml/neurite/montage_percell.py --overlay-only --run-id <run id> \
  --manifest <manifest> --raw-root <RAW_ROOT> --out-dir <OUT> --cache-dir <OUT>/cache --checkpoint <CKPT>

Run this inside a Slurm job, not on the dev node.

6. Output files and how to read them

OUT/
  runs/<timestamp>_<label>/
    percell.csv              one row per soma
    perwell.csv              one row per well
    params.json              every setting of this run
    <EXP>_<WELL>_<TP>_percell.tif   QC overlay, 4x downsampled (fresh GPU wells only)
  latest -> runs/<newest>
  cache/<EXP>_<WELL>_<TP>.npz      soma labels + neurite map (keep this)

percell.csv

ColumnMeaning
soma_idSoma label in the montage. Unique only inside one (experiment, well, timepoint).
area_px, cy, cxSoma area and centre (row, column) in montage pixels
neurite_len_pxTotal length of this soma's neurites (straight step = 1, diagonal = √2). 0 = no neurite.
skel_pxNumber of skeleton pixels (the unit CellProfiler uses)
n_branch_points, n_end_pointsBranch nodes and tips on this soma's neurites
n_primary_neuritesNeurites that leave the soma
max_branch_lengthLongest path from the soma along the neurite (px)

perwell.csv

ColumnMeaning
n_somas, n_somas_with_neuriteAll somas; somas with a neurite
total_len_px, mean_len_per_somaSum of lengths; sum divided by all somas (zeros included)
median_len_per_somaUsually 0, because most somas have no neurite. Do not use it for length.
mean_branch_points, mean_tips, mean_primary_neurites, mean_max_branch_len, frac_branchedAverages over somas with a neurite only

How we analysed the XDP data

  • Two readouts (agreed with Julia, October 2026): (1) length and branching among cells that have a neurite (neurite_len_px where skel_px > 0); (2) the fraction of cells with a neurite. The fraction of cells with no neurite changes a lot between experiments for technical reasons, so we did not use mean length over all somas.
  • Replicates: the cell line is the replicate for genotype; wells are not independent. Use a mixed model with experiment and cell line as random effects.
  • Units: pixels. For the IXM 20X objective with 1×1 binning, 1 px ≈ 0.348 µm (XDP1/3/5: 0.347534; XDP8/10/11: 0.348214). For other microscopes, read the pixel size from your image metadata (on IXM: spatial-calibration-x).
  • siRNA or drug is not in the output. Join it from your plate map on (experiment, well).

7. Settings

These are the settings of the final XDP run. The job scripts already use them. The input-layout settings are in section 5a.

OptionValueWhat it doesChange from cache?
--diameter25Expected soma diameter for Cellpose-SAM (px)No
--flow / --cellprob0.6 / −1.0Cellpose thresholdsNo

Run python ml/neurite/montage_percell.py --help (inside the container) for all options.

8. How the neurite model was trained (SNT hand tracing + clDice)

The neurite map comes from a small U-Net (a type of image-to-image neural network). We taught it what a neurite is by tracing neurites by hand in Fiji with the SNT plugin. You need this section only if you want to check the model on new data, or train a new model (for example for another microscope, objective or marker).

8a pick crops→ 8b trace by hand in SNT→ 8c traces → training masks→ 8d train (GPU)→ 8e score on held-out crops
The production model (run1)
Crops picked20 crops of 640×640 px from XDP5, 8, 10 and 12 tiles, balanced across genotypes and cell lines
Crops traced12 (all neurites in each crop, by Austin, in SNT)
Training / held-out10 crops for training; 2 crops held out for scoring (XDP5 H15, XDP8 I07)
ResultF1 = 0.645 on the held-out crops (Frangi filter: 0.135)

8a. Pick crops to trace

Tracing a whole 2048×2048 tile takes too long. Instead, pick_roi_crops.py picks one 640×640 crop per tile: the area with the most neurite-like signal and the least saturated cell bodies. It saves the raw crop (to trace) and a context image (the whole tile with a yellow box, for reference only).

Choose input tiles that cover your conditions: every genotype or cell line, several experiments, dense and sparse wells. Then run (CPU job):

sbatch --export=ALL,STEP=crops,TILES=/path/to/chosen/tiles,TRACE_DIR=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<lab>/<project>/neurite-tracing \
       ~/nextflow-cluster/ml/neurite/sbatch/neurite_trace_prep.sbatch

8b. Trace the neurites in Fiji (SNT)

Setup, once. SNT needs Java 21. Download Fiji “latest” with Java included (the -jdk download from imagej.net), then in Fiji: Help ▸ Update ▸ Manage update sites ▸ tick Neuroanatomy ▸ Apply, and restart Fiji. Copy the __ROI.tif files to your computer, or open them from the mounted HIVE share.

For each __ROI.tif:

  1. File ▸ Open the __ROI.tif. Image ▸ Adjust ▸ Brightness/Contrast ▸ Auto, so that faint neurites are visible.
  2. Plugins ▸ Neuroanatomy ▸ SNT..., and choose the open image.
  1. Trace one neurite at a time, from the soma to the tip:
    • Click on the edge of the soma where the neurite starts (1).
    • Click a bit further along the neurite (2). SNT finds the path along the bright line between your clicks and shows it. Press Y to keep it, or N to remove it and click again.
    • Go on clicking along the neurite (3, …). At the tip, press F to finish the path.
    • For a branch: hold Alt+Shift (Option+Shift on a Mac) and click on the existing path where the branch starts, then trace the branch the same way.
DoDo not
Trace every neurite inside the crop, the full length, with all branches. A complete crop teaches the model what is and is not a neurite. Trace only some neurites. Untraced neurites teach the model that they are background.
Follow the centre line of the neurite.Trace the somas. Cellpose finds the somas; trace only the processes.
Skip a faint smudge if you are not sure it is a neurite.Guess. A wrong trace is worse than a missing one in an unclear spot.
  1. Save: in the SNT window, File ▸ Save Tracings ▸ TRACES.... Use the same name as the crop, in the same folder, for example XDP5-RGEDI_H15_T6_t4__33113.2I__ROI.traces. (If SNT shortens the name at the first dot, that is fine: the next step matches it.)

About 10–15 traced crops is a good start; more is better. Variety (experiments, cell lines, dense and sparse areas) matters more than number.

8c. Turn the traces into training masks

rasterize_traces.py reads each .traces file, draws the paths as 1-pixel lines, and widens them to about 5 px (the target the network learns). It also writes a check image: the crop with the trace in magenta. Open every _qa.tif and confirm that the magenta lines lie on the neurites.

sbatch --export=ALL,STEP=rasterize,TRACE_DIR=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<lab>/<project>/neurite-tracing,DATA=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<lab>/<project>/neurite-training-data \
       ~/nextflow-cluster/ml/neurite/sbatch/neurite_trace_prep.sbatch

8d. Train the model

Training shows the network random 256×256 pieces of the traced crops (flipped, rotated, brightness changed) and adjusts it until its output matches the traces. Two crops are held out: the network never sees them, and they are used to score it.

Why clDice. A normal loss counts overlapping pixels, so a network can score well while it breaks neurites into pieces. The clDice loss compares the centre lines (skeletons) of the prediction and the trace, so a gap in a neurite costs a lot. That matters here, because we measure neurite length and branching per cell.

sbatch --export=ALL,DATA=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<lab>/<project>/neurite-training-data,OUT=/gladstone/finkbeiner/<lab>/<project>/neurite-model/run2,VAL=H15:I07 \
       ~/nextflow-cluster/ml/neurite/sbatch/neurite_train.sbatch
  • VAL: parts of the names of the held-out crops, joined by :. Choose at least 2 crops from different wells and cell lines.
  • INIT=<path>/run1/best.pt (optional): start from our model and adjust it to your data (fine-tuning). This needs fewer traced crops than training from zero.
  • Settings used for run1: 200 epochs × 200 steps, batch 8, 256×256 pieces, learning rate 0.001, U-Net depth 4 with 32 base channels (1.9 million weights), loss = clDice + weighted cross-entropy (positive weight 5). The job script uses them. The run1 job took 8 minutes on one V100; the best held-out score came at epoch 23, and that checkpoint is kept as best.pt.

8e. Check the model on the held-out crops

After training, the job scores the model and a classical Frangi filter on the held-out crops. The score is F1: the centre lines of the prediction and of your trace are compared, and a point counts as a match if it is within 3 px. F1 = 1 is perfect, 0 is no match. It also writes an image per held-out crop:

  • run1: F1 = 0.645 (Frangi 0.135). Faint neurites are hard for people too, so 1.0 is not reachable.
  • A new model is better only if it scores higher on the same held-out crops, and its overlays look right on whole wells.
  • To use a new model, pass CKPT=<OUT>/best.pt to neurite_run.sbatch, with a new cache folder (a new OUT). Results from a new model are not comparable with the frozen XDP results.

9. How we ran cluster jobs with Claude

Most of this module was built with Claude Code, an AI coding assistant. This is the way of working that we used. It is safe on a shared cluster.

Who does what

ClaudeYou
Reads code and data (read-only), writes and edits code, writes the .sbatch job script, reads logs and results, makes figures and reports. Submits every job (sbatch), cancels jobs (scancel), approves every write, decides what to delete, pushes code.
Rules we kept Claude never submits or cancels a Slurm job. No heavy work on the dev node. Raw data is read-only. Outputs go to the HIVE, never to the cluster home. Never push to or merge into main; it belongs to the whole lab. Work on your own branch made from austin-claude.

The loop

  1. Tell Claude what you want, for example: “Run the neurite module on wells B02–B12 of MYEXP at T5. The raw data is in <path>. Write outputs to <HIVE folder>.”
  2. Claude checks the input files over sft (read-only), works out the file pattern and grid, writes the manifest and a self-contained .sbatch script on your computer, and gives you one command to submit it.
  3. You run the submit command. It sends the script to the cluster and submits it: 
    base64 < ~/sbatch-claude/JOB.sbatch | sft ssh --command 'mkdir -p ~/<project> && cd ~/<project> && base64 --decode > JOB.sbatch && sbatch JOB.sbatch' fb-galaxy-dev01
    base64 turns the script into plain text, so it goes through the SSH pipe without quoting problems.
  4. Check the queue (all users, so you can see GPU contention): 
    sft ssh --command 'squeue -o "%.8i %.10u %.14j %.9P %.8T %.10M %.9l %.6D %.10b %R" -S -t,i' fb-galaxy-dev01
  5. When it is done, Claude reads the log and the CSVs over sft and reports the result.

Help for your own Claude sessions

  • CLAUDE.md in the repository root tells Claude the project rules, the cluster setup and this module. Claude Code reads it automatically when you start it in the repository folder.
  • .claude/skills/cluster-batch-submit/ in the repository teaches Claude the submit hand-off above.
  • Good first prompts: “Read docs/neurite_howto.html and CLAUDE.md, then help me run the neurite example test.” “My images are in <folder>. Work out the TILE_PATTERN, GRID, TILE_ORDER and OVERLAP_PX for the neurite module.” “Explain how montage_percell.py assigns a neurite to a soma.”
  • Ask for a plan before large changes. Read every change (git diff). Run the example test again after you change the code.

10. The other route: Nextflow + database module

bin/neurite_montage.py is the same method as a Nextflow pipeline step (DO_NEURITE_MONTAGE = true in the config). It reads tiles from the galaxy database and writes celldata and neuritecelldata rows instead of CSV files. It was tested on XDP5 (job 20554, 2026-09-04). Example config: configs/austin/finkbeiner-neurite-montage-XDP5.config.

cd ~/nextflow-cluster
python bin/validate_config.py <your.config>
sbatch --export=ALL,NEXTFLOW_INSTALL_DIR=$HOME/nextflow-cluster run.sh -c <your.config>
Use the CSV route for results that you compare with the XDP data. The database module does not have the root-contact attribution (--root-px, --cross-cos), the newer branch metrics or the input-layout settings of section 5a, so its numbers are not the same. It also needs an experiment that is registered in the database, and params.platemap_path must list your wells.

11. Limits, known problems, troubleshooting

What we know about accuracy

  • The neurite model was trained on 12 hand-traced crops of live RGEDI (EGFP fill) neurons, 20X, IXM, from four XDP experiments. Held-out F1 = 0.645. For a new microscope, marker, objective or cell type, look at overlays first. If possible, trace a few crops in SNT and score them (section 8). If the score is low, fine-tune the model with your traces (INIT=, section 8d).
  • Attribution is not perfect. In a check with fake somas (real masks moved to random places), we estimated that 14–24% of “has a neurite” calls are chance contacts in dense wells. Total length per well does not depend on attribution.
  • Live neurite images are faint and change between experiments. Fixed MAP2 staining traces much more cleanly, if your question allows fixed cells.
  • Most somas have no traced neurite, so medians are usually 0.

Troubleshooting

ProblemCause and fix
Job is PENDING (Resources) for hoursThe galaxy partition has only 2 GPU nodes (one V100 each). CPU jobs from other users can fill them. Wait, or ask the other user or IT.
SKIP: found N tiles (need M ...)The folder, TILE_PATTERN, well or timepoint does not match your files, or GRID is wrong. The message names the folder it searched. Compare it with ls of that folder.
site numbers repeatThe pattern matches more than one file per site (for example two channels or two timepoints). Make TILE_PATTERN more specific.
Montage looks scrambled (neurites jump at tile edges)Wrong TILE_ORDER or OVERLAP_PX. Try the other orders on one well and look at the overlay.
cache ... built with different paramsYou changed a soma setting, the tile layout or the checkpoint. Use a new cache folder.
Run is about 10× slower than expectedCellpose 4 must use use_bfloat16=False on V100 GPUs. The script already does this; keep it if you edit the code.
refuses to overwriteThe run folder exists. Use a new LABEL, or --overwrite if you are sure.
Bright bands or straight lines along tile edges in the overlaySeam effects (section 1a). Keep --seam-band 6 and --flatten-size 128. With overlapping tiles, also check OVERLAP_PX and TILE_ORDER.
ERROR: cannot read the container or Container not foundThe shared image is missing or you cannot read it. Check with ls -l /gladstone/finkbeiner/kaye/XDP/dev-nextflow-modules/nextflow-cluster.sif. If it is gone, rebuild it from nextflow-cluster.def (see docs/DEVELOPMENT.md).
Permission denied on the SIF or the modelYou are not in the finkbeinerlab group. Ask IT.
Test 1 failsYour checkout is not austin-claude, or the code was changed. Check git -C ~/nextflow-cluster status and the code: line at the top of the log.
SNT says “Java Upgrade Required”Your Fiji has an old Java. Install Fiji “latest” with Java 21 included (section 8b).
